category: Polymer Flow Module: Non-Newtonian, Viscoplastic and Viscoelastic Flow, Curing and Chemorheology
description: Rheology capabilities of the COMSOL Polymer Flow Module (and CFD Module): the Viscoelastic Flow interface with Oldroyd-B, Giesekus, FENE-P/FENE-CR, PTT and Rolie-Poly models, all inelastic non-Newtonian and viscoplastic (Papanastasiou-regularized) viscosity models of the Fluid Properties node with verified Java property names, thermal shift functions, non-Newtonian porous media flow, and the Curing Reaction interface with chemorheology for thermoset processing.

tools.name: Viscoelastic Flow (vef)
tools.description: Interface for incompressible flow of viscoelastic fluids (polymer melts and solutions, biological fluids): it solves continuity, the Navier–Stokes equations with an extra elastic stress and a hyperbolic constitutive transport equation (upper-convected derivative) for the elastic stress of one or more relaxation branches. Stationary and time-dependent analyses; boundary conditions mirror Laminar Flow, including free surfaces and moving walls.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Viscoelastic Flow (vef); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("vef", "ViscoelasticFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Constitutive relation
parameters.description: Viscoelastic (default), Newtonian or Inelastic non-Newtonian (Fluid Properties).

parameters.name: Material model
parameters.description: Oldroyd-B, Giesekus, FENE-P, FENE-CR, LPTT, EPTT or Rolie–Poly with multiple branches.

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: Stress (default) or conformation-based constitutive equation formulation.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid Properties, Initial Values, Wall, Gravity, Flow Continuity.

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module or CFD Module. High Weissenberg numbers need continuation in λ, P2 velocity, and often the conformation formulation for robustness.

tools.name: Fluid Properties (Viscoelastic Flow): Constitutive Relation and Branches
tools.description: Domain node of the Viscoelastic Flow interface defining density, solvent viscosity μ_s and the viscoelastic material model with a table of relaxation branches (polymer viscosity μ_e,m, relaxation time λ_e,m and model-specific parameters per branch), which approximates a relaxation spectrum. It also contains thermal effect functions and the discretization of the elastic stress (linear by default).
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties (fp1); Java: physics("vef").feature("fp1").set("Constitutiverelation", "Viscoelastic")

parameters.name: MaterialModelViscoelastic
parameters.description: OldroydB | Giesekus | FENEP | FENECR | LPTT | EPTT | RoliePoly.

parameters.name: Branch table
parameters.description: Viscosity, relaxation time and extra parameters per branch; load/save from text file.

tools.notes: Property names and model keys verified in COMSOL 6.4. Interior walls and pairs cannot separate Fluid Properties nodes with different branch counts.

tools.name: Oldroyd-B Model (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Simplest viscoelastic model (Hookean dumbbells in a Newtonian solvent): upper-convected Maxwell elastic stress plus solvent viscosity. It predicts elasticity and first normal stress differences but constant shear viscosity and unbounded extensional viscosity, so it is mainly used for Boger fluids and benchmarks such as flow past a cylinder.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties > Material model: Oldroyd-B (MaterialModelViscoelastic = OldroydB)
tools.notes: Unphysical in strong extensional flows (stress blow-up); use FENE-P or Giesekus there.

tools.name: Giesekus Model (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Viscoelastic model adding a quadratic stress term that represents anisotropic hydrodynamic drag between polymer molecules; the mobility factor α controls shear thinning, bounded extensional viscosity and a nonzero second normal stress difference. It fits semi-dilute and concentrated polymer solutions and melts well.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties > Material model: Giesekus (MaterialModelViscoelastic = Giesekus)
tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("vef").feature("fp1").set("MaterialModelViscoelastic", "Giesekus");
// GUI: branch table: viscosity 10[Pa*s], relaxation time 0.5[s], mobility 0.3
tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow or CFD Module.

tools.name: FENE-P and FENE-CR Models (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Finitely extensible nonlinear elastic dumbbell models: FENE-P (Peterlin closure) gives finite extensibility and shear thinning, FENE-CR (Chilcott–Rallison) keeps a constant shear viscosity with bounded extension. The extensibility parameter L² limits chain stretch, making them suited to dilute polymer solutions, drag reduction and filament stretching.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties > Material model: FENE-P (FENEP) or FENE-CR (FENECR)
tools.notes: Low L approaches Newtonian behavior; very large L approaches Oldroyd-B.

tools.name: Phan-Thien–Tanner Models LPTT and EPTT (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Network-theory models for polymer melts in which junction creation and destruction depend on stress: the linear (LPTT) and exponential (EPTT) forms give shear thinning and bounded (LPTT) or maximum-then-decreasing (EPTT) extensional viscosity controlled by the extensibility ε. They are popular for extrusion and die-swell simulations.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties > Material model: LPTT or EPTT

parameters.name: Extensibility ε (epsiloneLPTT)
parameters.description: PTT extensibility parameter (default 1 in GUI; typical 0.01-0.3).

tools.notes: Multi-mode EPTT fits of rheometer data are typical for melt processing.

tools.name: Rolie–Poly Model (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Tube-theory model for linear entangled polymers including reptation, chain stretch (Rouse relaxation time) and convective constraint release (CCR) with coefficient β and exponent δ. It captures stress overshoot and nonlinear extension of entangled melts better than single-mode differential models.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Fluid Properties > Material model: Rolie–Poly (RoliePoly)

parameters.name: CCR coefficient β (betaRoliePoly) and exponent δ

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module.

tools.name: Stress and Conformation Formulations (Viscoelastic Flow)
tools.description: Viscoelastic constitutive equations can be solved for the extra stress (default stress formulation) or for a conformation tensor, which improves positive definiteness and robustness at higher Weissenberg numbers. Consistent streamline/crosswind stabilization, pseudo time stepping for stationary solves and linear or higher-order elastic-stress shape functions are available.
tools.usage: Viscoelastic Flow > Viscoelastic Constitutive Equation Formulation (Show More Options) and Discretization section
tools.example:
// GUI: Viscoelastic Flow > Viscoelastic Constitutive Equation Formulation: Conformation
// Solve with a Parametric Sweep on the relaxation time from 0.01 s to the target value
tools.notes: See Solvers for Viscoelastic Flow and Pseudo Time Stepping for Viscoelastic Flow Models in the Polymer Flow User's Guide.

tools.name: Thermal Effects: Arrhenius and WLF Shift Functions (Polymer Viscosity)
tools.description: Temperature dependence of polymer rheology is introduced by a thermal shift function α_T(T) that multiplies solvent/polymer viscosities and relaxation times (viscoelastic) or the apparent viscosity (inelastic non-Newtonian and Darcy fluids): None, Arrhenius (activation energy), Williams–Landel–Ferry (C1, C2, reference temperature), exponential or user defined.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties (vef/spf/dl fluid) > Thermal Effects > Thermal function; Darcy fluid Java: feature("fluid1").set("thermalFunction", "shiftWLF")

parameters.name: WLF constants
parameters.description: C1 (C1wlf, default 8.86), C2 (C2wlf, default 51.6 K), reference Twlf.

parameters.name: Arrhenius
parameters.description: Activation energy Q and reference temperature T0.

tools.example:
// GUI: Laminar Flow > Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian: Carreau; Thermal Effects: Williams-Landel-Ferry, C1 = 17.44, C2 = 51.6[K], T_ref = 423[K]
// Couple temperature through Nonisothermal Flow (e.g., Polymer_Flow_Module/Tutorials/pasta_extrusion)
tools.notes: Thermal function names verified on the Darcy's Law Fluid node in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Nonisothermal Flow, Viscoelastic Flow (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface combining Viscoelastic Flow and Heat Transfer in Fluids through the Nonisothermal Flow coupling, with temperature-dependent viscoelastic properties and viscous/elastic heating. It is used for polymer extrusion, injection molding and coating where melt temperature controls rheology. Only incompressible flow is supported.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow > Viscoelastic Flow

parameters.name: Thermal effects
parameters.description: Arrhenius or WLF shift of relaxation times and viscosities.

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow or CFD Module.

tools.name: Inelastic Non-Newtonian Constitutive Relation (Laminar Flow)
tools.description: Option of the Fluid Properties node of Laminar/Creeping Flow (and the flow couplings) replacing constant viscosity by a generalized Newtonian model of the shear rate: Power law, Carreau, Carreau–Yasuda, Cross, Cross–Williamson, Sisko, Bingham–Papanastasiou, Herschel–Bulkley–Papanastasiou, Casson–Papanastasiou, DeKee–Turcotte–Papanastasiou, Robertson–Stiff–Papanastasiou, Ellis and Houska thixotropy. Parameters come from materials or user input.
tools.usage: Laminar Flow > Fluid Properties > Constitutive relation: Inelastic non-Newtonian; Java: feature("fp1").set("Constitutiverelation", "InelasticNonNewtonian"); set("nonNewtonianModels", "Carreau")

parameters.name: nonNewtonianModels
parameters.description: PowerLaw | Carreau | CarreauYasuda | Cross | CrossWilliamson | Sisko | BinghamP | HerschelBulkleyP | CassonP | DeKeeTurcotte | RobertsonStiff | Ellis | HouskaT.

parameters.name: *_mat switches
parameters.description: Each parameter has a *_mat property (from_mat or userdef).

tools.notes: Key names verified in COMSOL 6.4. Non-Newtonian laminar flow requires the CFD, Polymer Flow or Microfluidics Module; the rotating machinery interfaces support Power law, Carreau and the Papanastasiou viscoplastic models.

tools.name: Power Law Model (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Generalized Newtonian model μ = m (γ̇/γ̇_ref)^(n-1) with fluid consistency coefficient m and flow behavior index n (n < 1 shear thinning, n > 1 shear thickening); a lower shear-rate limit keeps the viscosity finite at zero shear. It fits many polymer solutions, slurries and food products over limited shear-rate ranges.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Power law (nonNewtonianModels = PowerLaw)
tools.notes: Predicts infinite viscosity at zero shear; the lower shear-rate limit is essential in stagnant regions.

tools.name: Carreau and Carreau–Yasuda Models (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Shear-thinning models with Newtonian plateaus: Carreau μ = μ∞ + (μ0 - μ∞)[1 + (λγ̇)²]^((n-1)/2) and Carreau–Yasuda with an additional transition parameter a replacing the exponent 2. They are the usual choice for polymer melts and blood-like fluids where both zero-shear and power-law regions matter.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Carreau / Carreau–Yasuda (nonNewtonianModels = Carreau / CarreauYasuda)

parameters.name: mu0 / mu_inf (Carreau)
parameters.description: Zero and infinite shear rate viscosity.

tools.notes: Blood (Cho & Kensey parameters) is a classic Carreau example.

tools.name: Cross and Cross–Williamson Models (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Shear-thinning models used heavily in injection molding: the Cross model (zero and infinite shear viscosities, power index and critical stress τ*, the stress at which thinning starts) and the Cross–Williamson model (zero-shear viscosity, relaxation time, power index). Combined with WLF or Arrhenius shift they form the Cross-WLF melt viscosity model.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Cross / Cross–Williamson (nonNewtonianModels = Cross / CrossWilliamson)
tools.notes: Add a thermal function (WLF) for Cross-WLF behavior of thermoplastics.

tools.name: Sisko Model (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Model combining a power law with an infinite-shear viscosity, μ = μ∞ + m (γ̇/γ̇_ref)^(n-1), describing the high-shear region of greases, paints and some food and personal-care products where the viscosity levels off at high shear rates.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Sisko (nonNewtonianModels = Sisko)

parameters.name: m_pows / n_pows
parameters.description: Consistency coefficient and flow behavior index.

tools.notes: Like the power law, it diverges at zero shear for n < 1.

tools.name: Bingham–Papanastasiou Model (Viscoplastic Flow)
tools.description: Viscoplastic model for fluids with a yield stress: μ = μ_p + τ_y (1 - exp(-m_p γ̇))/γ̇, where the Papanastasiou regularization parameter m_p smooths the unyielded/yielded transition so it can be solved as a generalized Newtonian fluid. It models toothpaste, drilling mud, concrete and slurries with plug flow.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Bingham–Papanastasiou (nonNewtonianModels = BinghamP)

parameters.name: m_p
parameters.description: Regularization (model) parameter, default 10 s; larger values approach ideal Bingham behavior.

tools.notes: Increase m_p gradually (parametric continuation) to avoid convergence problems.

tools.name: Herschel–Bulkley–Papanastasiou Model (Viscoplastic Flow)
tools.description: Yield-stress fluid with power-law behavior after yielding: μ = m (γ̇/γ̇_ref)^(n-1) + τ_y (1 - exp(-m_p γ̇))/γ̇. It describes food pastes, cement, muds and many suspensions more accurately than Bingham.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Herschel–Bulkley–Papanastasiou (nonNewtonianModels = HerschelBulkleyP)

parameters.name: m_p / sr_ref
parameters.description: Regularization parameter and reference shear rate.

tools.notes: Pipe Flow offers the Swamee–Aggarwal friction factor for Herschel–Bulkley fluids in 1D networks.

tools.name: Casson–Papanastasiou Model (Viscoplastic Flow)
tools.description: Regularized Casson model, √τ = √τ_y + √(μ_p γ̇), with Papanastasiou smoothing; widely used for blood at low shear rates, chocolate and printing inks.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Casson–Papanastasiou (nonNewtonianModels = CassonP)
tools.notes: Also available in the rotating machinery interfaces.

tools.name: DeKee–Turcotte and Robertson–Stiff–Papanastasiou Models (Viscoplastic Flow)
tools.description: Additional regularized yield-stress models: DeKee–Turcotte (exponential shear-rate dependence with shear rate viscosity μ_DK and relaxation time λ_DK) for food and biological suspensions, and Robertson–Stiff (power-law with yield, consistency m and index n) used for drilling fluids and cement slurries.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > DeKee–Turcotte–Papanastasiou (DeKeeTurcotte) / Robertson–Stiff–Papanastasiou (RobertsonStiff)
tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module.

tools.name: Ellis Model (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Stress-based shear-thinning model μ = μ0/(1 + (τ/τ_1/2)^(a-1)) with a Newtonian plateau at low stress; because it depends on stress, the apparent viscosity is solved implicitly and needs an initial guess μ_app,0. It suits dilute polymer solutions and biological fluids.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Ellis (nonNewtonianModels = Ellis)

parameters.name: tau_half
parameters.description: Shear stress at which viscosity is halved (default 1 N/m²).

parameters.name: mu_init_app
parameters.description: Initial guess of apparent viscosity (default mu0e).

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module.

tools.name: Houska Thixotropy Model (Non-Newtonian Flow)
tools.description: Time-dependent (thixotropic) viscoplastic model in which a structural parameter describes breakdown under shear and rebuilding at rest; yield stress and consistency each have permanent and thixotropic parts. It captures viscosity decrease with shearing time of gels, drilling muds, yogurt and 3D-printing pastes.
tools.usage: Fluid Properties > Inelastic non-Newtonian > Houska thixotropy (nonNewtonianModels = HouskaT)

parameters.name: nf / nb
parameters.description: Flow behavior index and breakdown index.

tools.notes: Needs a time-dependent study since the structure parameter evolves in time.

tools.name: Non-Newtonian Fluids in Porous Media (Apparent Shear Rate)
tools.description: Darcy's Law and Brinkman interfaces can use inelastic non-Newtonian viscosity models (power law, Carreau, Carreau–Yasuda, Cross, Cross–Williamson, Sisko) through an apparent shear rate γ̇_app = α |u| / sqrt(κ ε_p) that yields the same pressure drop as free flow. The correction factor α is user defined or from the capillary model (with constant C), for polymer flooding, filtration of polymer solutions and resin impregnation.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Porous Medium > Fluid > Constitutive relation: Inelastic non-Newtonian; Java: feature("porous1").feature("fluid1").set("Constitutiverelation", "InelasticNonNewtonian")

parameters.name: nonNewtonianModels
parameters.description: powerLaw | carreau | carreauYasuda | cross | crossWilliamson | sisko (Darcy fluid keys are lower camel case).

parameters.name: correctionCoefficient
parameters.description: userDef (alpha) or cap (capillary model with C, default 4).

parameters.name: thermalFunction
parameters.description: none, Arrhenius, WLF, exponential or user.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4 on the Darcy's Law Fluid node.

tools.name: Curing Reaction (creq)
tools.description: Interface for the degree of cure (conversion) c_r of thermosetting resins during heat treatment: a convection–reaction equation with temperature-dependent curing kinetics, in fluid domains (with a velocity field from a flow interface) or solid domains. It is used for composite curing, adhesives, potting and reaction injection molding in 1D to 3D.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Curing > Curing Reaction (creq); Java: physics().create("creq", "CuringReaction", "geom1")

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: Temperature field from a heat transfer interface.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid (CuringKinetics, ck1), No Flux, Initial Values.

parameters.name: Other nodes
parameters.description: Solid, Conversion, Open Boundary, Symmetry, Chemorheology.

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module. Add the Curing Reaction Heating coupling to feed the exotherm back into the heat equation.

tools.name: Curing Kinetics: n-th Order, Šesták–Berggren and Kamal–Sourour (Curing Reaction)
tools.description: Kinetic models of the Curing Reaction Fluid/Solid nodes for the cure rate dc_r/dt: n-th order (single Arrhenius rate), Šesták–Berggren autocatalytic and Kamal–Sourour (combined n-th order and autocatalytic with two Arrhenius constants). An optional diffusion factor or modified diffusion factor limits the rate near vitrification.
tools.usage: Curing Reaction > Fluid (ck1) > Curing Kinetics; Java: physics("creq").feature("ck1").set("kineticModel", "SestakBerggren")

parameters.name: reactionRateLimiter
parameters.description: noneModel | diffusionFactor | modifiedDiffusionFactor (cr_c, Cd, cr_f, Cf).

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. Calibrate parameters from DSC data with Parameter Estimation.

tools.name: Chemorheology (Curing Reaction)
tools.description: Node of the Curing Reaction interface relating resin viscosity to degree of cure and temperature: a viscosity factor from the Castro–Macosko model (gel point, constants c1, c2) or a percolation model (gel point, exponent) multiplies a base viscosity (Newtonian, power law or Cross) with a thermal function. The resulting viscosity can be used by the flow interface during filling and curing.
tools.usage: Curing Reaction > Chemorheology; Java: physics("creq").create("crh1", "Chemorheology", 3)

parameters.name: Viscosity factor
parameters.description: Castro–Macosko (gel point, c1, c2) or Percolation (gel point, exponent p).

parameters.name: Compute effective transport properties
parameters.description: Newtonian, Power law or Cross base viscosity.

parameters.name: Thermal function
parameters.description: Temperature shift of the base viscosity.

tools.notes: Viscosity diverges at the gel point; stop the flow simulation before gelation.

tools.name: Curing Reaction Heating (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling that adds the exothermic curing heat source Q = ρ H_r dc_r/dt from the Curing Reaction interface to the heat equation, capturing thermal runaway and exotherm peaks in thick composite laminates and castings.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Curing Reaction Heating (default name crh1)

parameters.name: Heat of reaction H_r
parameters.description: Total heat released per unit mass (J/kg).

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module.

tools.name: Solid and Conversion (Curing Reaction)
tools.description: Solid node (SolidCuringKinetics) applies the curing kinetics in solid domains without convection (e.g., prepreg laminates in an autoclave), and the Conversion boundary condition prescribes the degree of cure at inlets (fresh resin) or other boundaries.
tools.usage: Curing Reaction > Solid (domain) / Conversion (boundary); Java: physics("creq").create("solid1", "SolidCuringKinetics", 3); create("conv1", "Conversion", 2)

parameters.name: Kinetic model
parameters.description: Same options as the Fluid node.

parameters.name: Conversion c_r0
parameters.description: Prescribed degree of cure on the boundary.

tools.notes: Type ids from the COMSOL 6.4 plugin registry.

tools.name: Parameter Estimation for Rheological Models (Polymer Flow)
tools.description: Workflow for calibrating non-Newtonian, viscoelastic and curing model parameters against rheometer or DSC data with the Parameter Estimation study step and a Global Least-Squares Objective. The Polymer Flow Module provides the BOBYQA (derivative free), IPOPT and Levenberg–Marquardt solvers for this step.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Optimization > Parameter Estimation; Study > Parameter Estimation step

parameters.name: Experimental data
parameters.description: Table/file with shear rate vs. viscosity, or time vs. conversion.

parameters.name: Estimated parameters
parameters.description: e.g., mu0, lam_car, n_car with bounds and scales.

tools.example:
// GUI: Component > Definitions > Global Least-Squares Objective (load viscosity curve)
// Study > Parameter Estimation: parameters mu0 (1e-3..1e3 Pa*s), n_car (0.1..1), method Levenberg-Marquardt
tools.notes: The Optimization Module offers more solvers and general optimization features.

tools.name: Polymer Processing Application Library Models (Polymer Flow Module)
tools.description: Tutorial models shipped with the Polymer Flow Module that show complete processing setups: pasta and polymer extrusion (non-Newtonian nonisothermal flow), internal mixer (rotating machinery with non-Newtonian melt), rubber injection molding and 2D/3D slot-die coating (phase field two-phase with non-Newtonian liquids), resin transfer molding (Brinkman + level set in porous media) and viscoelastic FSI.
tools.usage: File > Application Libraries > Polymer Flow Module > Tutorials / Verification Examples

parameters.name: pasta_extrusion
parameters.description: Laminar Flow + Heat Transfer, Carreau with temperature shift.

parameters.name: internal_mixer
parameters.description: Rotating machinery laminar flow of a polymer melt.

tools.notes: Application Library model names verified in the local COMSOL 6.4 installation.

tools.name: Two-Phase and Three-Phase Flow with Non-Newtonian Fluids (Polymer Flow)
tools.description: With the Polymer Flow Module the Two-Phase Flow, Level Set; Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field; Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh and Laminar Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field interfaces accept non-Newtonian models for one or all phases (power law, Carreau, Bingham/Herschel–Bulkley/Casson–Papanastasiou), which is needed for coating, injection molding filling, dispensing of pastes and food processing. The moving mesh variant cannot handle topology changes such as droplet pinch-off.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field (or Level Set) > Fluid 1 / Fluid 2 > Dynamic viscosity: non-Newtonian model; Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow

parameters.name: Fluid 1/Fluid 2 viscosity model
parameters.description: Newtonian or one of the inelastic non-Newtonian models per phase.

parameters.name: Interface tracking
parameters.description: Level set, phase field or moving mesh.

parameters.name: Surface tension
parameters.description: Library or user coefficient in the coupling.

tools.notes: Only incompressible fluids are supported in these two-phase interfaces.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Laminar Flow of Polymer Melts (Polymer Flow)
tools.description: The Polymer Flow Module includes the Rotating Machinery, Laminar Flow interface with non-Newtonian (and creeping-flow) support, so internal mixers, extruder screws sections and kneaders with rotating rotors can be modeled with Frozen Rotor or time-dependent sliding-mesh studies, optionally nonisothermal with viscous heating.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Rotating Machinery > Rotating Machinery, Laminar Flow; Java: physics().create("spf", "LaminarFlow", "geom1"); common().create("rot1", "RotatingDomain")

parameters.name: Constitutive relation
parameters.description: Inelastic non-Newtonian (e.g., Carreau with WLF shift).

tools.notes: Requires the Polymer Flow Module (or Mixer/CFD Modules).
